To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the long distance contribution to the $m_{K_L}-m_{K_S}$ mass difference can be determined non-perturbative, that the long distance part is small compared to the short distance part, and that the short distance part is dominated by the charm quark contribution.

the long distance contributions to $K_{S}^{0}-K_{L}^{0}$ mass difference can be computed with a high degree of precision, that they are large and negative and that the dominant long distance contributions come from the $K\to\pi\pi$ and $K\to 3\pi$ transitions.
the long-distance part of the $K_{S}$-$K_{L}$ mass difference is 2.1(2) MeV, and the long-distance part to $\varepsilon'$ is 1.4(1.4) $\times 10^{-3}$.

the long-distance part of the mass difference is consistent with zero within our statistical errors.

we have determined the $K_{0}$-$\overline{K^{0}}$ mass difference in the chiral limit, with a residual pion mass of 420 MeV and a residual kaon mass of about 559 MeV, to be 3.3 MeV with an error of 1.1 MeV.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of a lattice calculation of the $K_{0}$-$K_{0}$ mass difference using the GIM mechanism to eliminate the largest part of the short distance lattice artifacts and RI/MOM technique to eliminate the rest.
